title: a-superseded-intention-is-never-silent
intention: Let an intention be superseded or deprecated as a MACHINE-READABLE state, and make that state impossible to pass silently while boats ride it: the deprecating hand gets a report of what is riding (with its own blindness declared), and any boat still riding is refused at its next forward crossing, naming the supersession.
why: Akien, 2026-08-18, reasoning from the graph trees: 'if an intention got superceeded or otherwise depricated, we'd have to also review it's children or in flight whatevers.' Then the correction that shaped the build — 'the ticket is supposed to say what it's intention is already, so that IS the link back, yes?' It is. `owning_intention` is the edge and reversing it is a scan over a directory, so NO BIDIRECTIONAL LINK IS BUILT: the graph tree needed both directions because it is large and in a database; 162 files in git do not, and a stored back-edge would be a second copy of a fact that already exists, with two writers and a drift mode. THE GAP WAS NEVER THE LINK — it is that nothing traverses it and, more basically, that nothing can be superseded at all. MEASURED 2026-08-18: zero of 56 charters carry any supersession or deprecation state; 21 mention the words somewhere in prose, which is exactly the shape `owner` had before `gated_by` — the fact exists in English and nothing can read it. So there is no event, and with no event the only remaining mechanism is a sweep, which is the drift this system names by hand.

falsifier.proves_green: PROOF GATE: tester — proofs beside the code at cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/, run twice, sealed under TesterDevice().run_proof with isolation='netns', VALIDATION persisted beside the code. RED FIRST IS REQUIRED: the proof must fail on the unmodified tree on exactly the arms the defect owns, or the green is evidence about the fixture. ENTRY: buildme_rides_the_chart (a berthed validate packet claiming this ticket). EXIT: proved_answers_the_chart (a complete passing verdict artifact). EMISSION: WatchmeEmissionRed (the probe armed before the WATCHME crossing). CLEARANCE: harbor_master.clearance.clear for the forward crossing into PROVED — owning intention is cairn/devices/harbor_master/intention+why.json, verified 2026-08-18 to carry gated_by and so not among the 41 charters that would refuse.
falsifier.proves_red: Mark an intention superseded while a boat rides it, then: (a) that boat's next forward crossing REFUSES, naming the supersession and the successor; (b) the deprecation-time scan names that boat; (c) that scan reports how many in-flight tickets it could NOT attribute. Any of the three missing kills it. WRONG-SHAPE, the specific hollow: the scan reports 'no boats riding, clear to supersede' while in-flight tickets carry no owning_intention — a green earned by not being able to see. Today that would be a clean report over 28 boats with 44 invisible. SECOND WRONG-SHAPE: the supersession recorded by editing the charter's existing prose in place, so a record of truth is rewritten to say it was always this way.
falsifier.horizon: the first live supersession of an intention that has boats riding it

how: THREE PIECES, and the second is the one that makes the third honest. (1) STATE: charters gain a machine-readable supersession field — the successor's address and the date — written as an ADDITION, never by rewriting the charter's existing prose to say it was always this way (the discipline ruling-door-supersede-path established for ruling packets, cited rather than extended). (2) THE REVERSE READ WITH ITS BLINDNESS DECLARED: harbor_master gains `boats_riding(intention_address)` — the reverse of `boat_owner_of`, same discipline (files only, no daemon, no registry, no network), returning both the boats it found AND the count of in-flight tickets it could not attribute because they carry no `owning_intention`. A scan that reports only what it found is the exact hollow this node exists to forbid. (3) THE REFUSAL, AT A DOOR THAT IS ALREADY OPEN: harbor_master.clearance already resolves boat -> ticket -> owning_intention -> charter -> gated_by, so it is already holding that charter open. It reads one more field. A boat whose owning intention has been superseded is refused at its next forward crossing, naming the supersession and the successor. NOT AT THE CHARTER-WRITE DOOR, and the reason is load-bearing: recompile_gate.sh never blocks its caller and always exits 0 by charter, because that is what makes it safe to fire on every write — putting a refusal there would destroy the property that makes it usable.
